messages.subject: Re: smart vs dumb quotes in docs cause errors
messages.subject_clean: smart vs dumb quotes in docs cause errors
messages.body_plain:
Hi Cindy,

I'm pretty sure I won't change this since single quotes and double quotes in R are interchangeable. And I don't recommend copying and pasting from a PDF document, as you've found out PDF readers do weird things surrounding copy/paste. Rather, use the internal documentation from within R. You should have no problems copying and pasting either the HTML or internal formats.

Best,

Jeff

On Sun, Aug 5, 2012 at 1:14 PM, CB <cindyb...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Hi all,
>
> Thanks Jeff for this fantastic package and the complete documentation.
>
> I found a small error regarding the use of single quotes in the documentation, http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/Rook/Rook.pdf
>
> It uses single quotes,   '   ,  for character strings and variable names. However, they get rendered in the pdf as curly left-handed or smart quotes. R interprets these are "commas". So when I copy/paste the example code from the pdf into R, I get errors. For example:
>
>
> >  copied from the pdf:
>
> >  <https://lh4.googleusercontent.com/-w_aRPTI3Up8/UB60vMit1WI/AAAAAAAAAB4/n7P3TwywQyI/s1600/curlyexample.tiff>
>
> >  pasted into the R console, and hit enter
>
> >  <https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/-3ZGiKjxRqnE/UB6vhmbCOkI/AAAAAAAAABo/wdzQ9_ZXIeA/s1600/curlyexampleR.tiff>
>
> > comma, easily missed by newbies, is R's interpretation of the code, and the explanation of the error:
>
> > > Error: unexpected input in "system.file(‚"
>
> > code typed by hand and hit enter, gives correct result:
>
> >  <https://lh4.googleusercontent.com/-VzQ8lezKziM/UB624KKt8VI/AAAAAAAAACA/uVN1Owo7dH4/s1600/curlyexampleRgood.tiff>
>
>
> I know this is a small thing to experienced programmers, and not a problem if you type the code by hand, but it caused me hours of frustration as I was trying to learn Rook by copy/pasting large blocks of code, ie, on pages 13-14.
>
> To fix it in your next version of the docs,it probably has something to do with the word processing settings: perhaps use "dumb" instead of "smart" quotes.
>
> I think Rook is fantastic. Hope this helps,
>
> CB
